text:
Alexandre Texier has found a home in Montreal's bottom six, and Eric Engels of Sportsnet wrote about his confidence; Arpon Basu of The Athletic wrote about his secret to puck protection. He has five points in 17 games at 13 minutes a night, including a goal against Pittsburgh.

The underlying numbers are better than the points. Montreal has 58% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, more than seven points better than without him, and he has two goals on 3.3 expected. The team has also scored three fewer goals than expected with him out there, so he's due a little.

He's from Grenoble, a second-round pick by Columbus in 2017 who went through St. Louis before landing with the Canadiens. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season while facing tough competition (95th percentile). Our projection sees about 14 goals. On a Canadiens team missing centers, a winger who protects the puck and tilts the ice is worth more than his line suggests.
